arxiv-2012-03873.title: Continuous dynamical decoupling of spin chains: Inducing two-qubit interactions to generate perfect entanglement
arxiv-2012-03873.creator: Abdullah Irfan, Syed Furqan Abbas Hashmi, Syeda Neha Zaidi, Muhammad Usman Baig, Wahaj Ayub, Adam Zaman Chaudhry
arxiv-2012-03873.description: Abstract Efficient control over entanglement in spin chains is useful for quantum information processing applications. In this paper, we propose the use of a combination of two different configurations of strong static and oscillating fields to control and generate near-perfect entanglement between any two spins in a spin chain, even in the presence of noise.

arxiv-2110-10504.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sofiane Bouarroudj a,∗ , Dimitry Leites a,b , Irina Shchepochkina c. The Bol operators are unary differential operators between spaces of weighted densities on the 1-dimensional manifold invariant under projective transformations of the manifold.

arxiv-2201-08207.title: Invasion Dynamics in the Biased Voter Process
arxiv-2201-08207.creator: Loke Durocher, Panagiotis Karras, Andreas Pavlogiannis, Josef Tkadlec
arxiv-2201-08207.description: Abstract The voter process is a classic stochastic process that models the invasion of a mutant trait A A (e.g., a new opinion, belief, legend, genetic mutation, magnetic spin) in a population of agents (e.g., people, genes, particles) who share a resident trait B B , spread over the nodes of a graph.

arxiv-2207-00094.title: Optimal Quantum Control of Charging Quantum Batteries
arxiv-2207-00094.creator: R. R. Rodríguez, B. Ahmadi, G. Suárez, P. Mazurek, S. Barzanjeh, P. Horodecki
arxiv-2207-00094.description: Abstract Quantum control allows us to address the problem of engineering quantum dynamics for special purposes. While recently the field of quantum batteries has attracted much attention, optimization of their charging has not benefited from the quantum control methods. Here we fill this gap by using an optimization method.

arxiv-2309-16869.title: Vidaptive: Efficient and Responsive Rate Control for Real-Time Video on Variable Networks
arxiv-2309-16869.creator: Pantea Karimi Sadjad Fouladi ⊞ \boxplus Vibhaalakshmi Sivaraman Mohammad Alizadeh Massachusetts Institute of Technology , ⊞ \boxplus Microsoft Research
arxiv-2309-16869.description: Abstract . Real-time video streaming relies on rate control mechanisms to adapt video bitrate to network capacity while maintaining high utilization and low delay. However, the current video rate controllers, such as Google Congestion Control (GCC), are very slow to respond to network changes, leading to link under-utilization and latency spikes.

arxiv-2311-12897.title: A Compact Dynamic 3D Gaussian Representation for Real-Time Dynamic View Synthesis
arxiv-2311-12897.creator: Kai Katsumata, Duc Minh Vo, Hideki Nakayama
arxiv-2311-12897.description: Abstract 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has shown remarkable success in synthesizing novel views given multiple views of a static scene. Yet, 3DGS faces challenges when applied to dynamic scenes because 3D Gaussian parameters need to be updated per timestep, requiring a large amount of memory and at least a dozen observations per timestep.

arxiv-2407-20858.title: Planar network statistics for two-dimensional rupturing foams
arxiv-2407-20858.creator: Joseph Klobusicky, Elif Onat, Vasilios Konstantinou
arxiv-2407-20858.description: Abstract We conduct experiments on a class of two-dimensional semiwet foams generated through compressing a three-dimensional soap foam between two glass plates. To induce a spatially uniform rupturing process on foam boundaries, an additional plate is heated and placed on top of the unheated plates.

arxiv-2410-11348.title: RATE: Causal Explainability of Reward Models with Imperfect Counterfactuals
arxiv-2410-11348.creator: David Reber, Sean M. Richardson, Todd Nief, Cristina Garbacea, Victor Veitch
arxiv-2410-11348.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David Reber, Sean M. Richardson, Todd Nief, Cristina Garbacea, Victor Veitch. Reward models are widely used as proxies for human preferences when aligning or evaluating LLMs. However, reward models are black boxes, and it is often unclear what they are actually rewarding. In this paper, we develop Rewrite-based Attribute Treatment Estimator (RATE) as an effective method for measuring the sensitivity of a reward model to high-level attributes of responses, such as sentiment, helpfulness, or complexity.

arxiv-2412-13133.title: Analyzing Toxicity in Open Source Software Communications Using Psycholinguistics and Moral Foundations Theory
arxiv-2412-13133.creator: Ramtin Ehsani, Rezvaneh (Shadi) Rezapour, Preetha Chatterjee
arxiv-2412-13133.description: Abstract Studies have shown that toxic behavior can cause contributors to leave, and hinder newcomers’ (especially from underrepresented communities) participation in Open Source Software (OSS) projects. Thus, detection of toxic language plays a crucial role in OSS collaboration and inclusivity.

arxiv-2602-07267.title: BRIDGE: Predicting Human Task Completion Time From Model Performance
arxiv-2602-07267.creator: Fengyuan Liu Jay Gala Nilaksh Dzmitry Bahdanau Siva Reddy Hugo Larochelle
arxiv-2602-07267.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Fengyuan Liu Jay Gala Nilaksh Dzmitry Bahdanau Siva Reddy Hugo Larochelle. Evaluating the real-world capabilities of AI systems requires grounding benchmark performance in human-interpretable measures of task difficulty. Existing approaches that rely on direct human task completion time annotations are costly, noisy, and difficult to scale across benchmarks. In this work, we propose BRIDGE, a unified psychometric framework that learns the latent difficulty scale from model responses and anchors it to human task completion time.

pmc-10542784.title: Proof-of-concept study linking ex vivo sensitivity testing to neoadjuvant anthracycline-based chemotherapy response in breast cancer patients
pmc-10542784.creator: Marjolijn M. Ladan, Titia G. Meijer, Nicole S. Verkaik, Cecile de Monye, Linetta B. Koppert, Esther Oomen-de Hoop, Carolien H. M. van Deurzen, Roland Kanaar, Julie Nonnekens, Dik C. van Gent, Agnes Jager
pmc-10542784.description: We developed a functional ex vivo anthracycline-based sensitivity test. Surgical resection material of primary breast cancer (BC) was used to determine criteria for the ex vivo sensitivity assay based on morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Subsequently, a proof-of-concept study was performed correlating results of this assay on primary BC biopsies with in vivo response after treatment with anthracycline-containing neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC).

pmc-10573821.title: Application of Nanotechnology in Plant Genetic Engineering
pmc-10573821.creator: Kexin Wu, Changbin Xu, Tong Li, Haijie Ma, Jinli Gong, Xiaolong Li, Xuepeng Sun, Xiaoli Hu, Amy L Klocko, Jianjun Chen, Haiwei Lu
pmc-10573821.description: The ever-increasing food requirement with globally growing population demands advanced agricultural practices to improve grain yield, to gain crop resilience under unpredictable extreme weather, and to reduce production loss caused by insects and pathogens. To fulfill such requests, genome engineering technology has been applied to various plant species. To date, several generations of genome engineering methods have been developed.

pmc-11538836.creator: Li Yao, Fuhong Wu, Hua Mu, Xinli Wang, Juan Liu, Hongyan Lu
pmc-11538836.description: BackgroundHealth literacy refers to individual skills to access, process, understand, and use health information to stay healthy. This study explored the mediating effect of health literacy on social support and self-care ability in older patients undergoing percutaneous coronary stent implantation (PCI).
